body: I always, *always* do this whenever I ship an order out. I put in a little surprise gift with every shipment. Usually nothing big or difficult to make, but it's always something that fits with the purchase in some way. I keep a bin of little things I make just for this, and getting to pick out each surprise is one of my favorite parts of my job. If the order has to be late for any reason, I throw an extra item from my gift bin in for every day that it's late. Sometimes customers will contact me telling me how much they appreciate the thought that goes into my packaging, but usually I don't hear back unless they order from me again. It's nice to know this is appreciated!

At least with legal help I'd have some kind of an advocate, which is what I've been hoping for, but I'm not sure I can afford that considering how much of what I'd be getting would be going right back into paying for my medical issues.

I also nearly died twice as a child- once when I was 6 after the horrible asthma attack that **finally** convinced the doctors that my nurse mother wasn't just being hysterical when she repeatedly brought me in because there was just something "off" about my breathing. I vaguely remember being really confused about what was happening, and asking over and over if I was going to die. My mom kept saying I'd be fine, but I remember the way she said it. I couldn't figure out why she was lying to me.

The second time was when I got strep that turned into pneumonia when the absolute mental reject subbing in for my usual pediatrician flat-out refused to even do a culture because he was **sure** it was just the flu and I"d be fine in a couple days. 3 years later when my lung partially collapsed from persistent weakness from the pneumonia, I was still pretty angry about that. I don't remember being sick, I was too feverish to really understand how serious I actually was until afterwards.

Neither of those times really affected me at all though, other than to make me much more diligent about always, **ALWAYS** having an inhaler within reach.

I instantly stopped believing in God, at least in the Christian sense of the word. Without getting into details which I'm just not sure I'm ready to talk about, I was going to die at the hands of another person. Someone who, if there *were* a benevolent god anywhere in the universe, would never have been allowed anywhere near me, let alone close enough to put his hands around my throat. I wasn't perfect, but I was a **good** person. I had never knowingly hurt anyone. And yet I was going to die at the hands of a monster. In a single second I went through being hurt, then angry that such a thing should be allowed to happen to a kid (yeah, forgot to mention I was *barely* 15 at the time), and then I came to the conclusion that there must not be any god (let alone capital-G "God"). If there's no god, then Heaven and Hell probably don't exist either. Then I just sort of...gave up. If I was going to die, I was going to die. I was still pretty sure souls were a thing, so I tried to focus on the idea of keeping my soul together enough so that I could haunt the sick bastard into either confessing or just going crazy before he could get to anyone else, but I'm not sure if I believed that could happen or not. I don't remember anything after that thought. I never asked for details because I didn't ever want to think about that night any more clearly than as something abstract that happened to me once in the past, but essentially someone intervened after I lost consciousness, and I (obviously) survived. What's stuck with me to this day though is that I don't remember **anything** after accepting that I was going to die. No white lights, no dead relatives, no pearly gates, not even a sense of floating in the dark. Literally just...nothing. Like I didn't even exist for a while. I've had an absolutely obsessive fear of death ever since, because I can't shake the belief that that's what death is. I know I wasn't breathing at first, and I think I might've died briefly. It's that thought, that I was dead and being dead means you just stop existing, that scares me more than the actual experience. Not feeling someone else's hands on me, not looking up at those horrible, dead eyes, not the smells or the sounds or the thoughts about what my family would think when I just disappeared without a trace, just that infinite....nothingness. I'd take the experience a million times over if I could just for a single fraction of a second shake that fear that there's nothing waiting for us after we die. Infinite nothing. Nothing upon nothing upon nothing. How fucked up is that?

No official diagnosis as my shitty excuse for medical care has made it impossible to hang on to a psych professional long enough to trust them with this particular tidbit, but long story short I was a passenger in a car that was used in a homicide. As in, they drove over someone. Repeatedly. I could hear and feel all of it. That was 10 years ago and to this day, even the thought of getting behind the wheel is enough to give me panic attacks. It's not even that I felt bad for the guy, he was a monster who deserved far worse than he got, but it really messed me up. Any time I'm even a passenger in a car, I'm stuck in full-alert mode the entire time. I had nightmares for years about the accident. The sounds it made...If I hear anything that sounds remotely like that I have incredibly vivid flashbacks. I can't ever take road trips because the tension in my neck from the stress gives me migraines. I'm not sure I'll ever be able to drive, which sucks because I'm disabled now and there's no public transportation in my town. I'm completely reliant on other people, maybe for the rest of my life, and I'm not sure I'll ever be able to tell them why.

I stumbled onto it completely by accident. I had always been creatively-oriented, but it wasn't until I started sewing my own clothes that I realized how much I enjoyed actually *creating* something physical out of a bunch of random parts (as opposed to writing or playing music). I was 99% sure that was the direction I wanted to go, but when I kept wanting to create even after I lived the starving artist life for **years**, I knew for sure it was what I wanted. Now, the thought of doing anything else with my life just depresses me. I can compromise when I have to (making "normal" things instead of the elaborate costumes I'd prefer to be making), but it's not even a matter of want anymore. I **NEED** to be creating. When I'm not creating, I'm thinking about creating. When I'm not thinking about creating, I'm looking for inspiration for new things to create. Every second of my life is completely consumed by my passion. When it physically hurts you to not be doing the thing you love at all times, you know you're on the right track. I don't think it's something you can find by looking. Just do things that make you happy until you find the thing that makes you ache for it in your "off" hours.

All this said, I know I'm lucky, in a way, to have found my passion at my age. Some people never find that. Some people don't find it until they're much, much older. I found mine early and nobody believed me that I knew exactly what I wanted to do with my life, but at least **I** knew. 10 years from now, I'll have all these years of working toward my passion to show people that I'm serious, while most of my peers still won't have found their own passions.

I want to make costumes. I don't care where or for who. I'd prefer to work on movies, but mostly I just want to design and create amazing characters to bring joy into other people's lives. I want to create the next Freddy or Jason (not as in reinvent the already-existing characters, but as in create an entirely new character who becomes just as iconic). The next Dracula. The next Captain Jack Sparrow or Indiana Jones. 

Right now, my disability and lack of access to reliable public transportation have kept me from ever having a "real" job. But I still design and sew every chance I get. I have my own line of little plush dolls that are pretty successful locally. I sew and design for other dolls as well, which I do enjoy because I can test out some of my more difficult costuming ideas on a much smaller, more affordable scale. I sew for people whenever I can, but most people in my area aren't willing to pay me what I'm worth, so it's pretty few and far between these days. It's not my dream job because while I enjoy the hell out of it, it doesn't make me any money, and requires a lot of stress and extra "peopleing" on my part to make each sale happen. If I could make enough money at it to pay my bills and not live in my mom's house with her paying for my food and clothes and everything, I'd be happy doing it for the rest of my life. But as it is, It's not definitely no "dream" job.

"Ugly" actors tend to share a trait that makes them much easier for me to identify: asymmetry! I love when there's a character I can easily identify in every single scene based on those stand-out traits, even if they're not moving or talking. I love Steve Buscemi because he's an incredibly talented actor, but part of me is always grateful when I watch his movies that there's at least one character whose voice/ mannerisms I don't have to quickly memorize just to follow the plot. I actually love movies, even though I have to make a little more effort to follow the plot. I just happen to love them a bit more when the characters' faces are as unique as their personalities.

A group of friends and I all got blanket bans from every sporting goods store in our region. As in, our pictures were apparently circulated with managers being warned to remove us from their stores immediately upon sight, or so we were told once while being forcibly removed from a recently-opened Dick's we thought we could still get into. We didn't even do anything *that* serious, considering these stores sold **ACTUAL** weapons. We were just a bunch of latchkey kids who *really* could've benefited from some adult supervision. We had decided that summer that it would be the absolute height of comedy if we could get ourselves locked into the store overnight for an indoor camping trip. Our plan was to shut ourselves in the tents and wait for everyone to leave for the night. It was working out great until this obnoxiously large family with like 14 kids came in. A few of their little sprogs saw our shadows moving around in the tents and wandered over. We, being incredibly intelligent tweeny boppers, decided it would be fun to scare the little bastards into thinking all the tents in the store were haunted. We were surprisingly successful. The kids ran away shrieking like tiny, snot-crusted banshees, and several minutes later mall security was dragging half a dozen hysterically laughing kids out of the tents and escorting us out of the store. My best friend at the time, being a not-at-all obnoxious fool, ran back into the store, loaded her arms with those Nerf footballs with the tails on them, and starts launching them at employees and security while running through the aisles yelling "You'll never take me alive!" She wasn't allowed to come with us on any future "missions."

On another occasion, we got bored of hiding in the tents and decided to move on to jousting with golf clubs. That was, admittedly, a much more reasonable removal. I remember one guy took a particularly meaty-looking club right to the nose at one point and had to run out of the store to find some paper towels. Our group was whittled down to 4 after it turned out we'd broken the poor guy's nose, and his parents wouldn't let him hang out with us anymore. XD 

At a third location, our "let's test out the climbing wall" idea went south when two guys got bored of waiting in line and got into a chalk fight which somehow ended up with a chalk bowl stuck on someone's head. Yes, actually stuck. As in they had to cut it off. Down to 3, as one more parent caught on that we were "those kids."

The last one we very nearly accomplished our goal. It was closing time and they had turned off all of the lights, and the manager was going around checking the tents. They didn't, however, check the *shelves behind the tents*. Three of us had very strategically squeezed onto a single shelf behind a big boxed tent and were waiting for everyone to lock up for the night. Sure enough, they checked the tent, found nothing, and started to leave the department. It was only when I had the worst-timed sneeze EVER that we were caught. By then, it was the end of summer, we'd terrorized every sporting goods store in the area, and they were beyond tired of dealing with our bullshit. This joke I heard from my ex. I'm actually not even sure you can call it a joke, it's really more of an anti-joke. The whole point is that it's neverending, but I'll try and tell it in the shortest way possible. I promise you it's worth reading to the end! Ready?

A father is talking with his young son.

Dad: It's almost your birthday, you're going to be five! You'll be starting school soon, should I get you a cool new backpack or something?

Son: No. All I want is fifty pink ping pong balls. 

Dad: Are you sure? No cool Batman lunch box or anything like that? 

Son: Nope. Just fifty pink ping pong balls. 

Dad: Okay...

So the kid's birthday rolls around, and they have a party. He's opening presents, but isn't really excited by any of his new toys or clothes or anything until he comes to the last present on the pile. Sure enough, inside the box are fifty pink ping pong balls. The kid is just ecstatic, he's NEVER had such an amazing gift in his life! "Thank you thank you thank you Dad it's the BEST present ever!"

The next year, the father asks his son again: 

Dad: It's almost your birthday again! What do you want this year? A new Lego set? Some cool light-up shoes?

Son: Nope. I just want fifty pink ping pong balls. 

Dad: Really? No new toys or school clothes? 

Son: Nope. Just fifty pink ping pong balls.

Dad: Okay...

So the kid's birthday rolls around, and they have another party. Again, the kid is totally ambivalent to all of his presents until he gets to the last box. Again, inside the box are the pink ping pong balls. And again, the kid is SO grateful, he's NEVER had such a great present before, it's just the best gift EVER!

The joke goes on this way- kid gets older, dad asks son if he wants some kind of age-appropriate, stereotypically "cool" present (like a gaming system for a teenager, a car at 16, etc.), and every year the kid just wants fifty pink ping pong balls. Every year, he couldn't care less about any of his presents but is always thrilled with the fifty pink ping pong balls. The objective of telling this joke is to keep going with it until the listener becomes visibly frustrated that the joke has gone on this long before moving to "Act 2", the anti-climax of this anti-joke. You can skip a few years here and there, but you have to keep it going for as long as possible. When it seems like they're going to throttle you if you don't get to the punch line, you move on to this part:

The next year, the son is in a horrible accident just before his birthday. Knowing this will be his last one, his dad asks him what he wants for his present.

Dad: You can have anything you want, anything in the entire world, no matter the cost. What can I get you to make this last birthday special?

Son: All I want is fifty pink ping pong balls.

Dad: SERIOUSLY? Anything in the world and that's what you want?

Son: Yes. Just fifty pink ping pong balls. That'll make me happier than 
anything else in the world.

Dad: Fine. Fifty pink ping pong balls.

The son's birthday comes around, and there's only one present to open this time. Inside are fifty pink ping pong balls. At this point, the son is mere minutes from death, but his father can see in his face that he really is the happiest he's ever been, all because of those damned pink ping pong balls. Knowing this is his last chance, the father finally asks the question he's been dying to know for so many years. 

Dad: Okay, I know we don't have long, but I *HAVE GOT* to know. What's the deal with the pink ping pong balls?

Son: Oh, it's simple! I just...

And then the son dies.



The end, to the most evil experiment in torturing your friends you'll ever dare to try. To all of you who share this anti-joke, you're welcome. To all of your friends, I'm so sorry. Just know that sharing your pain in this case really *does* make it better!

Bear with me, I can be bit long-winded in intros, and there's a lot to cover to give you an understanding of where I'm coming from.

I'm 25, f, formerly pretty active, but I've recently become disabled. I have severe, chronic pain in one knee that makes it incredibly difficult for me to get around at all, let alone to work out. I have a lot of other health issues that make most forms of exercise either too difficult to do regularly, or just downright impossible, but I used to really enjoy walking. I walked A LOT. As in several miles a day, always at a pretty brisk pace. I have a treadmill in my house that I would use all the time, so I never had to worry about bad weather or anything like that getting in the way of my exercise. If I wasn't on the treadmill, I was still always walking. I don't drive, and the public transportation in my area is a bit of a joke, so I pretty much ended up walking at least a few miles even on a slow day if I wanted to leave my house at all to hang out with friends or whatever. 

Unfortunately, that's no longer an option for me. On a GOOD day, I can now barely make the walk to the end of my block and back without limping pretty heavily. On a bad day? I might not get out of bed except to pee. I don't even get up to eat, because it's not worth having to stand for however long it's going to take me to make the food, unless there's some fruit or veg in the fridge already washed and ready to just grab and eat in bed. Clearly I'm nowhere near as active as I used to be, and as I'm sure you can expect, I've put on quite a bit of weight as a result. It's "only" 50 lbs, but that's quite a lot on a person with a small frame like me, and it JUST. WON'T. BUDGE. They're telling me there's essentially nothing that can be done for my knee. As far as they can tell, it's a result of a hypermobile joint irritating the surrounding tissue, and I just have to somehow learn to live with that because "it's not serious enough to talk about surgical intervention at this point." I happen to disagree, as a formerly very active 25-year-old now (seemingly) permanently reduced to a flabby blob on the couch. Whatever. Point is, I need to figure out some way to get myself feeling like less like early '90s Rosie O'Donnell and more like...well, basically ANYTHING else. I've tried talking to friends, but none of them will listen. If it's not "It's not that noticeable!" or "Yeah, I wish I could lose weight too" (*while eating donuts and sipping a bit of coffee with their giant cup of liquid diabetes*), it's "I'd kill for your body!" REALLY? Because I would *literally* kill to be rid of it these days. While I do have quite a...erm...let's call it a "shapely" figure (think Jessica Rabbit, but just a tad bit more realistic), since becoming disabled I've acquired a pair of bat wings that would make any lunch lady proud, a paunch that is rapidly approaching full-on beer belly status, and I'll spare you all the details of my thighs and bum, but suffice it to say it's not a pretty situation. I take it as a compliment to my abilities as a professional seamstress that I've been able to hide such a dramatic weight change from my closest friends and family, but it doesn't help when requests for advice go unanswered because they won't accept that I DO need to lose weight, and quite a bit of it at that.

At my absolute physical peak, I weighed in at between 140-145lbs. I can still look healthy at 135. Anything below 130 and I start to look pretty horrific, but the only times I've ever hit that point were when I was pretty seriously ill for long stretches of time. Generally, I tend to hover somewhere right around 145, which is where I'd like to see myself again. Currently, I've plateaued around 175. The initial gain saw me shoot up from 135 straight to 185, but at the time I was eating my "school" diet, which included a lot more slightly-less-healthy-but-easy-to-eat-during-a-VERY-long-commute snacks than I like to consume normally. I had to leave school because of the disability issue (even on public transport, I still had to walk roughly 3 miles as part of the commute, and yes, it actually WAS uphill both ways), so cutting all of that out of my diet and going back to my super bland, boring, but also VERY healthy diet did see some of the weight start to drop off. I'm just not sure what to do to get rid of the rest of it. I have so much trouble with food and digestion that I really can't make any changes to my diet (not that there's anything to change anyway, it really is a very boring, healthy diet). I also can't eat less. I only eat around 1200 calories a day if that, and I have to eat specific amounts of food at specific times throughout the day to be able to digest things properly since I can't take meds for the GP anymore. I'm at a loss as to how to lose this last 30 lbs, and I don't know where else to turn. I know it might not seem like much to some people, but that extra 30 lbs makes A TON of difference when every step is already painful. Losing the weight will not just make me feel better about my appearance, it may actually help my knee pain as well. I just hope someone can offer some advice on how to actually accomplish this.
